findings.title: Lookup can match several rows when belief_time is NULL, so `scalar_one_or_none` raises.
findings.body:
The unique constraint on (content, start, belief_time, source, type) does not cover rows where `belief_time` is NULL, because PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct. Under the old lookup, which matched on `end`, posting the same label again with a different end and no belief time inserted a new row. Existing databases can therefore hold several rows that differ only in `end`.

The new filter turns `belief_time == None` into `IS NULL` and drops `end`, so it now matches all of those rows. `scalar_one_or_none()` then raises `MultipleResultsFound`, and the request fails with the same HTTP 500 this PR is meant to fix. This is a common case, since many annotations (for example holidays and API posts without a belief time) have no belief time.

Fix: when several rows match, pick one deterministically, e.g. `.order_by(Annotation.id).limit(1)` with `.scalars().first()`. Or handle the NULL case separately and keep `end` in the filter there. I could not confirm whether `belief_time` is nullable or gets a default value in this model.
